app.title: Radiowriter: Literature and drafting for Radiopaedia articles
app.summary: The person searches a bibliographic database, either with a one-line query or by building it in blocks of synonyms. Section headings and imaging modalities can be turned into ready-made search terms, and a filter preset can be added. They look through the hits ranked by citation counts or journal rank, and save the ones they choose to a local archive, a reading list or a draft's references. They then screen the archive card by card: they mark each article read or flagged, sort it into reading lists, delete it, or open and save its full-text PDF to highlight in a reader. Finally they write the article in a Markdown editor that inserts the recommended section structure, numbers the citations, checks the text against the publisher's style rules, and copies the formatted article and its reference list or exports the draft as a file.

task.text: Find, screen and keep the published literature behind a reference article, and draft that article with numbered citations in the publisher's required structure and style.

data.text: Bibliographic records fetched from a literature database, with abstracts, journal metrics, citation counts and open-access links. Around them are the person's reading lists, read and flagged marks, full-text PDFs with highlights, a search history and a Markdown draft that cites the records by identifier.
data.item: a bibliographic record of one published article (title, authors, journal, abstract, identifiers)

stage.text: screening search results for a reference article, then writing it up with citations

mechanism.text: Four numbered tabs form a pipeline. A query builder feeds a paged list of result cards that are saved into an archive. The archive is screened as cards with read, flagged, list and delete controls under filters for status, list, text and journal quartile. Saved PDFs open in a reader where highlights become a checklist of cards. In the writing tab a Markdown editor sits next to a references sidebar that pulls in flagged or listed articles, and below them are a formatted preview, a linter and rich-text copy boxes.

field.text: literature searching and screening for a radiology reference article

workflow.name: search the literature, screen the hits, and draft a cited article from the ones kept

steps.here: A PubMed query is typed on one line or built in blocks (synonyms OR'd, concepts AND'd). Article headings and imaging modalities can be added as ready-made MeSH and text-word strategies. A three-position switch sends a recent-reviews preset, no filters or custom filters, and 🔎 Search PubMed fetches the records.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Results are sorted by influential citations, total citations, citations per year, recency or journal SJR, and narrowed by journal quartile. Each card is ticked 💾 Save, and the ticked cards go to the archive, to a reading list or to a draft's references.

steps.step: decide keep or drop for each item, with a reason
steps.here: In Screening each archive card is marked ✅ Read or ★ Flagged, or deleted with 🗑 Delete, singly or in bulk. Filters cover status, list, a title/abstract/PMID search and quartile. Articles marked read are removed at the next start unless they are in a list or have a PDF.
Named reading lists, for example one per article section, are created, renamed and deleted. An article can be ticked into several lists from its card.

The free PDF is saved, or a downloaded one is dropped in and matched by DOI or title, and renamed after the citation. It opens in a reader where selected text is highlighted in a colour. Each highlight becomes a card with a note and a done tick, stepped through with previous, next and done-and-next.

A Markdown draft gets the section headings recommended for its kind of article and cites with [@identifier]. Its reference list is filled from flagged articles, a reading list or typed identifiers, and the citations are resolved to formatted references.

The draft is linted against the publisher's style rules. The article HTML, with citations numbered by first appearance, and the reference lines are copied as rich text, and the draft can be exported as .json or .md.

distinctive: Hits are ranked by influence and venue: citation counts per year from a citation service and journal quartile and SJR from a bundled journal-ranking table.
The headings an article type requires are turned into search strategies, and the same section structure is later inserted into the draft and checked for misplaced headings.
Articles marked read are purged at startup unless they are kept in a list or have a PDF, and their identifiers are remembered so later searches skip them.
Citations are written as identifiers and numbered only at export, by order of first appearance. Duplicate identifiers for the same paper are merged, and listed-but-uncited references are reported.
A linter applies the publisher's transcribed style rules (contractions, spelling, acronyms, citation syntax) to the draft before it is copied as rich text into the publisher's editor.
